term: on the spur of the moment
ipa: ɑːn ðə ˈspɜːr əv ðə ˈmoʊmənt
respell: ahn thuh SPUR uhv thuh MOH-muhnt

senses.gloss: Suddenly, without planning ahead.
examples: We decided to drive to the coast *on the spur of the moment*.
I bought the jacket *on the spur of the moment* and regretted it later.
*On the spur of the moment*, he asked her to marry him.

ru: по дороге, по пути; на подходе
modifies: verbs of stopping and moving; *be* in *help is on the way*
contrast: *On the way* means during a trip; *in the way* means blocking someone (*Your bike is in the way*); *by the way* introduces a side remark. Russian *по дороге* is *on the way*, never *by the way*.

senses.gloss: While traveling somewhere; during the trip.
examples: Let's grab coffee *on the way* to work.
I called my mom *on the way* home.
We got lost twice *on the way*.

senses.gloss: Coming soon; about to arrive or happen.
examples: Stay calm, help is *on the way*.
They have two kids and a third *on the way*.

type: viewpoint — a general judgment that allows exceptions
position: front — also mid between commas or end
contrast: *On the whole* sums up a judgment (в целом); *as a whole* follows a noun and means taken together: *the country as a whole*.

senses.gloss: Generally; taking everything into account.
examples: *On the whole*, the trip went well.
The reviews were, *on the whole*, positive.
People here are friendly *on the whole*.

modifies: verbs of arriving, leaving, paying, finishing
contrast: *On time* means at the scheduled time, not late; *in time* means early enough, before it is too late: *The train left on time*, but *We got there in time to say goodbye*. Russian *вовремя* covers both.

senses.gloss: At the scheduled time; not late.
examples: The flight left *on time*.
Please pay your rent *on time*.
She's never *on time* for meetings.

type: frequency — one more time, often as before
modifies: a verb or a whole clause

senses.gloss: One more time; as has happened before.
examples: *Once again*, the bus was late.
Thank you *once again* for your help.
He has *once again* forgotten my birthday.

position: end — sometimes before the verb it follows

senses.gloss: Finally and completely, so it never has to be done again.
examples: Let's settle this *once and for all*.
I want to quit smoking *once and for all*.
The court ruling ended the dispute *once and for all*.

modifies: a verb or a whole clause

senses.gloss: Sometimes, but not often.
examples: We eat out *once in a while*.
*Once in a while* I still think about her.
It's good to take a day off *every once in a while*.

modifies: a verb or a whole clause

senses.gloss: One more time; again.
examples: Could you say that *once more*, slowly?
Let's go through the plan *once more*.
*Once more*, the team came back from behind.

senses.gloss: In a series, each following the one before.
examples: The guests left *one after another*.
Problems kept coming up *one after another*.
She ate three cookies *one after the other*.

senses.gloss: Singly, each separately after the last.
examples: Please come in *one at a time*.
Take the pills *one at a time*, with water.
Let's deal with these problems *one at a time*.

senses.gloss: Separately and in turn, one following another.
examples: *One by one*, the lights in the building went out.
The teacher called the students up *one by one*.
We checked the boxes *one by one*.

type: degree — very, often with a note of regret
position: before its word — an adjective or *well*
contrast: Not *only* plus *too*: *I'd be only too happy to help* means very happy, not excessively happy. With *well*, *aware* or *true* it adds regret: *I know that only too well* (увы, слишком хорошо).

senses.gloss: Very, completely; sometimes with regret that it is so.
examples: I'd be *only too* happy to help.
She knew *only too* well what would happen.
The danger is *only too* real.

ru: иначе, а то; а не то (пеняй на себя)
position: front — of the second clause, after a comma; alone at the end as a threat
contrast: It joins two clauses like a conjunction: *Hurry up, or else we'll be late*. Standing alone at the end (*Pay up, or else!*) it is an open threat, so avoid it in polite requests.

senses.gloss: Otherwise; if not, then something bad will happen.
examples: Wear a jacket, *or else* you'll freeze.
We need to leave now, *or else* we'll miss the train.
You have to pay by Friday, *or else* you lose your spot.

senses.gloss: Used alone at the end as a threat of punishment.
senses.ru: а не то пеняй на себя
examples: Be home by midnight, *or else*!
You'd better return my car, *or else*.

position: after its word — right after a number or amount
modifies: numbers and amounts of time, money, people
contrast: *About* and *around* go before the number; *or so* goes after it: *about ten minutes* = *ten minutes or so*.

senses.gloss: Approximately; a little more or less than the amount given.
examples: I'll be there in twenty minutes *or so*.
The repair cost a hundred dollars *or so*.
There were fifty people *or so* at the party.

senses.gloss: Outside, in front of a building.
examples: I'll wait for you *out front*.
There's a taxi *out front*.
Park *out front* and come in.

senses.gloss: In the leading position, ahead of the others.
examples: She stayed *out front* for the whole race.
The company wants to be *out front* on new technology.

type: manner — so that others can hear
modifies: verbs of reading, saying, laughing, thinking
contrast: *Out loud* means audibly, not silently; it does not mean *loudly*. *Aloud* means the same and is more formal.

senses.gloss: In a voice others can hear, not silently.
examples: Read the sentence *out loud*.
I laughed *out loud* at his message.
Sorry, I was just thinking *out loud*.

contrast: *Get out of hand* (выйти из-под контроля) uses the same words as an adjective-like complement: *The party got out of hand*. After *reject* or *dismiss* it means immediately, without thinking about it.

senses.gloss: Immediately and without serious thought, of rejecting something.
examples: The board rejected the proposal *out of hand*.
Don't dismiss the idea *out of hand*.
She refused his offer *out of hand*.

ru: вне поля зрения, с глаз долой
type: place — where it cannot be seen

senses.gloss: In a place where it cannot be seen.
senses.ru: вне поля зрения, с глаз долой
examples: Keep your valuables *out of sight* in the car.
The plane climbed until it was *out of sight*.
*Out of sight*, out of mind.

ru: ни с того ни с сего, как гром среди ясного неба

senses.gloss: Suddenly and without any warning.
senses.ru: неожиданно, ни с того ни с сего
examples: An old friend called me *out of the blue*.
*Out of the blue*, she announced she was moving to Texas.
The job offer came *out of the blue*.

contrast: Hyphenated before a noun it is an adjective meaning remote: *an out-of-the-way village*. *Go out of your way* means to make a special effort.

senses.gloss: Not blocking someone's path.
examples: Get *out of the way*!
Could you move your car *out of the way*?
Keep the cables *out of the way*.

senses.gloss: Finished, so it no longer needs attention.
examples: Let's get the paperwork *out of the way* first.
Once the exams are *out of the way*, we can relax.

senses.gloss: From nowhere, as if by magic; with nothing to base it on.
senses.ru: из ничего, из воздуха, откуда ни возьмись
examples: The deer seemed to appear *out of thin air*.
You can't just make up numbers *out of thin air*.
The money didn't come *out of thin air*.

position: end — usually right after *born* or *have a child*

senses.gloss: To parents who are not married to each other.
examples: He was born *out of wedlock*.
Having a baby *out of wedlock* is common now.
The share of children born *out of wedlock* has risen.

type: frequency — one more time, from the beginning
contrast: Americans often drop *again*: *Do it over*, *start over*. In British English *do it over* can mean *attack* or *redecorate*.

senses.gloss: Once more, from the beginning.
examples: I lost the file and had to write it all *over again*.
If I could live my life *over again*, I'd travel more.
Let's start *over again*.

type: frequency — many times in a row

senses.gloss: Many times, again and again.
senses.ru: снова и снова, раз за разом
examples: The kids watched the same movie *over and over*.
I've told you *over and over again* to lock the door.
She kept repeating his name *over and over*.

contrast: *Over here* and *over there* point to a spot the listener should look at; plain *here* is less pointed. *Over* does not mean *above* here.

senses.gloss: In or to this place, close to the speaker.
examples: Come *over here* and look at this.
Your keys are *over here* on the table.
Hey, we're *over here*!

type: manner — for each person, in statistics
modifies: verbs of spending, earning, using; numbers
contrast: Before a noun it works as an adjective: *per capita income*. As an adverb it follows the verb or figure: *spends more per capita*.

senses.gloss: For each person in a population.
examples: The US spends more on health care *per capita* than any other country.
The state collects about $3,000 in taxes *per capita*.
Coffee consumption *per capita* is highest in Finland.

position: after its word — right after the noun, or at the end
modifies: a noun or a whole statement, often negative

senses.gloss: By itself; in its own nature, apart from other things.
examples: Money *per se* doesn't make people happy.
I'm not against the plan *per se*, just the timing.
The drug isn't dangerous *per se*.

position: before its word — or mid (*I pretty much agree*)
contrast: *Pretty* here means *fairly*, not *beautiful*. Informal; in writing use *almost* or *nearly*.

senses.gloss: Almost; very nearly.
examples: I'm *pretty much* done with the report.
The two phones are *pretty much* the same.
He *pretty much* lives at the gym.

type: linking — rephrasing what was just said

senses.gloss: In other words; said another way.
examples: Sales fell by half. *Put differently*, we lost a million dollars.
*Put differently*, the problem isn't the price but the quality.
Or, *put another way*, nobody wants to pay for it.

contrast: *Right* here means *directly*, not *correctly*. British English also says *straight away*; Americans say *right away*.

senses.gloss: Immediately, without delay.
examples: I'll call you back *right away*.
We knew *right away* that something was wrong.
If you see smoke, leave the building *right away*.

position: end — almost always after *get off*, *go* or *walk away*

senses.gloss: Without being punished or paying for what you did.
examples: The real criminals got off *scot-free*.
He crashed my car and walked away *scot-free*.
It isn't fair that she went *scot-free*.

ru: пока, до сих пор; до определённой степени
position: front or end — mid with the present perfect (*has so far refused*)
modifies: a whole clause; with *only*, verbs of trusting or going
contrast: In the *until now* sense American English still prefers the present perfect: *So far we've sold 200 tickets*. Russian *пока* also means *for now* and *bye*, which *so far* never does.

senses.gloss: Up to now; until this moment.
examples: *So far*, so good.
We've had no problems *so far*.
The police have *so far* made two arrests.

senses.gloss: Only to a limited degree, usually with *only*.
senses.ru: до определённой степени, лишь до некоторой степени
examples: I trust him only *so far*.
Money can only take you *so far*.

type: viewpoint — flags a word used loosely or figuratively
modifies: a word or phrase just used

senses.gloss: Used to show that a word is not meant exactly or literally.
examples: He's the black sheep of the family, *so to speak*.
We're all in the same boat, *so to speak*.
The new manager is, *so to speak*, still learning the ropes.

senses.gloss: Before long; sooner or later, as you would expect.
examples: Don't worry, you'll find a job *soon enough*.
*Soon enough*, the kids were fast asleep.
He'll learn the truth *soon enough*.

position: before its word — an adjective or verb
modifies: adjectives, verbs, whole answers (*“Did you like it?” “Sort of.”*)
contrast: *Kind of* means the same. *A sort of* + noun is a noun phrase meaning a type of (*a sort of soup*), not the adverb. Informal; often written *sorta* in dialogue.

senses.gloss: Somewhat; in a way; to some degree.
examples: I *sort of* like him.
The room was *sort of* dark and cold.
It *sort of* makes sense, I guess.

contrast: Hyphenated before a noun it is an adjective: *step-by-step instructions*.

senses.gloss: Gradually, one stage at a time.
examples: The video explains the process *step by step*.
We rebuilt the business *step by step*.
Take it *step by step* and don't rush.

type: viewpoint — using a word in its exact meaning

senses.gloss: If you use words in their exact, correct sense.
examples: *Strictly speaking*, a tomato is a fruit.
*Strictly speaking*, we're not allowed to park here.
It's not, *strictly speaking*, a new idea.

type: manner — with the highest academic honors
contrast: American colleges use three levels: *cum laude* (with honors), *magna cum laude* (with high honors) and *summa cum laude* (with highest honors). It is not the same as a Russian *красный диплом*, which has one level.

senses.gloss: With the highest honors, of graduating from a college.
examples: She graduated *summa cum laude* from Yale.
Only five students finished *summa cum laude* this year.
He graduated *magna cum laude*, not *summa cum laude*.

position: front — with a comma, or end

senses.gloss: As expected or predicted; and in fact.
examples: I said it would rain, and *sure enough*, it poured.
*Sure enough*, the store was closed when we got there.
I checked the drawer, and there it was, *sure enough*.

type: linking — introduces a more exact restatement
position: front — of the restatement, or mid between commas
modifies: a clause or phrase that explains what came before

senses.gloss: In other words; used to explain or correct what was just said.
examples: We'll meet next week, *that is to say*, on Tuesday.
He's a vegan, *that is to say*, he eats no animal products.
The results were mixed; *that is to say*, not very good.

type: degree — at all, in negatives and questions
position: before its word — an adjective, after *not*

senses.gloss: At all; even slightly, in negatives and questions.
examples: I'm not *the least bit* worried.
She didn't seem *the least bit* surprised.
Are you *the least bit* interested in what I think?

type: manner — in the reverse order or relation
modifies: a clause describing an order or relation
contrast: Russian *наоборот* has three English equivalents: *the other way around* (the reverse is true), *vice versa* (and the reverse too) and *on the contrary* (you are wrong, the opposite is true). *“Are you tired?” “On the contrary!”* not *“The other way around!”*

senses.gloss: In the opposite order, direction or relation.
examples: I thought she was helping him, but it was *the other way around*.
You put the batteries in *the other way around*.
The dog doesn't walk me; it's *the other way around*.

contrast: Despite *again*, it does not mean *one more time*. *But then again, …* weighs a second point against the first.

senses.gloss: On the other hand; used to add a point against what was just said.
examples: The car is expensive. *Then again*, it'll last for years.
He might come, but *then again*, he might not.
I didn't love the movie, but *then again*, I'm not a fan of horror.

position: after its word — after a noun, or at the end
modifies: nouns of identity (*a New Yorker*), verbs like *soaked*, *know*

senses.gloss: Completely, in every part or way.
examples: She's a New Yorker *through and through*.
We were soaked *through and through*.
I know this city *through and through*.

position: front or end — mid with the present perfect
contrast: A formal *so far*, common in news and reports; in conversation say *so far*.

senses.gloss: Up to this point in time.
examples: *Thus far*, no one has claimed responsibility.
The results *thus far* are encouraging.
The company has *thus far* refused to comment.

modifies: a verb or a whole clause

senses.gloss: Repeatedly; many times.
examples: I've warned him *time and again*.
*Time and again*, the team has proven the critics wrong.
She makes the same mistake *time and time again*.

type: degree — too much of a good quality
position: after its word — right after an adjective

senses.gloss: To an excessive degree, of a quality that is usually good.
examples: My grandmother was generous *to a fault*.
He's honest *to a fault* and can't keep a secret.
The staff are polite *to a fault*.

position: front or end — also mid between commas
modifies: a verb or a whole clause

senses.gloss: Largely; in many ways.
examples: Our success depends *to a great extent* on the weather.
*To a great extent*, the report is accurate.
Prices are set, *to a large extent*, by demand.

type: degree — less than the thing just named
position: any position — often between commas before the last item
modifies: the last item in a list or a whole clause

senses.gloss: Less than something else that was mentioned.
examples: The storm hit Florida and, *to a lesser extent*, Georgia.
Kids, and *to a lesser extent* adults, love the game.
The same is true, *to a lesser extent*, of smaller cities.

type: degree — every single one, without exception

senses.gloss: Every one of them, without exception.
examples: The players backed their coach *to a man*.
The voters, *to a man*, rejected the plan.
They were, *to a man*, exhausted after the march.

senses.gloss: Exactly; perfectly.
examples: That dress fits you *to a T*.
The description matched him *to a T*.
She had his accent down *to a T*.

type: direction — first one way, then the other
contrast: Mostly written and a little old-fashioned; in everyday American speech say *back and forth*.

senses.gloss: Backward and forward; first one way, then the other.
examples: The branches swayed *to and fro* in the wind.
He paced *to and fro* outside the room.
People hurried *to and fro* across the square.

type: viewpoint — giving a more exact detail
position: front or end — or mid between commas
modifies: a whole clause or a detail

senses.gloss: Used to give more exact information.
examples: We've been married for ten years, eleven *to be precise*.
*To be precise*, the meeting starts at 9:15.
He isn't a doctor; he's a nurse, *to be precise*.

type: stance — concedes a point before a *but*
position: front or end — or mid between commas
contrast: Formal; it admits something before arguing the other side, and a *but* usually follows. It is not *to make sure* (чтобы убедиться).

senses.gloss: Admittedly; it is true, though something else matters more.
examples: *To be sure*, the plan has risks, but it's our best option.
The hotel was expensive, *to be sure*, but worth it.
There are, *to be sure*, a few problems left.

senses.gloss: As the first point or reason.
examples: *To begin with*, we can't afford it.
I don't like the job. *To begin with*, the hours are terrible.

senses.gloss: At first; at the start.
examples: I didn't like him *to begin with*, but now we're friends.
Why did you agree *to begin with*?

position: end — always last in the clause
modifies: a whole clause, adding one more thing
contrast: Nothing to do with a *boot* (ботинок) or with booting a computer.

senses.gloss: In addition; as well.
examples: She's smart, funny, and a great cook *to boot*.
The apartment was tiny and expensive *to boot*.
He lost his job and his car broke down *to boot*.

ru: на сегодняшний день, до сих пор
position: end — or front with a comma
modifies: a whole clause, usually in the present perfect; a superlative (*her best work to date*)
contrast: Not *up to date* (современный, актуальный): *the report to date* is the report so far, but *an up-to-date report* is a current one. Like *so far*, it takes the present perfect.

senses.gloss: Up to now; until the present time.
senses.ru: на сегодняшний день, до сих пор
examples: *To date*, no one has claimed responsibility for the attack.
The fund has raised $2 million *to date*.
This is her best album *to date*.

type: manner — to a customer's own request
contrast: Unrelated to *in order to* (чтобы). Before a noun it is hyphenated: *made-to-order furniture*.

senses.gloss: Specially for a particular customer, when they ask.
examples: All our sandwiches are made *to order*.
The table was built *to order*.
He has his suits made *to order*.

senses.gloss: Perfectly; exactly as well as possible.
examples: The steak was cooked *to perfection*.
She played the role *to perfection*.
The plan worked *to perfection*.

ru: в этом духе, примерно такого содержания
position: end — often in *something to that effect* or *words to that effect*

senses.gloss: With that general meaning, though not in exactly those words.
senses.ru: в этом духе, примерно такого содержания
examples: He said he was busy, or something *to that effect*.
There was a sign *to that effect* on the door.
She called me a liar, or words *to that effect*.

ru: в этом смысле, в этой мере
type: degree — as far as that goes

senses.gloss: In that respect; as far as that point goes.
senses.ru: в этом смысле, в этой мере
examples: The plan saves money, and *to that extent* it's a success.
*To that extent*, I agree with you.
He was only following orders, and *to that extent* he's not to blame.

type: manner — saying or showing the opposite
position: after its word — right after a noun like *evidence*, or at the end
contrast: *To the contrary* follows a noun or verb: *evidence to the contrary* (доказательства обратного). *On the contrary* opens a reply that rejects what was just said: *“Was it boring?” “On the contrary, I loved it.”*

senses.gloss: Showing or saying the opposite.
examples: Despite rumors *to the contrary*, the store is staying open.
Unless you hear *to the contrary*, the meeting is at noon.
There's no evidence *to the contrary*.

type: degree — completely, as far as possible

senses.gloss: Completely; to the fullest possible degree.
examples: Their house is mortgaged *to the hilt*.
I'll back you *to the hilt*.
He played the villain *to the hilt*.

type: manner — exactly as written or told
modifies: verbs of following, obeying, carrying out

senses.gloss: Exactly, paying attention to every detail.
examples: Follow the instructions *to the letter*.
She obeyed the rules *to the letter*.
We carried out the plan *to the letter*.

ru: не на жизнь, а на смерть; изо всех сил

senses.gloss: Very fiercely, with all your strength.
senses.ru: не на жизнь, а на смерть; изо всех сил
examples: Residents fought the new highway *tooth and nail*.
The two teams battled *tooth and nail* for the title.
She'll fight *tooth and nail* to keep her job.

ru: в данных обстоятельствах, в такой ситуации
contrast: Americans say *under the circumstances*; *in the circumstances* is more British. Russian *при таких обстоятельствах* does not become *at* or *by the circumstances*.

senses.gloss: Because of the situation; considering what has happened.
senses.ru: в данных обстоятельствах, в такой ситуации
examples: *Under the circumstances*, we had no choice.
You did the best you could *under the circumstances*.
The team played well *under the circumstances*.

type: time — already started and in progress

senses.gloss: Started and now in progress.
examples: Work on the new bridge is well *under way*.
The meeting got *under way* at ten.
Plans are *under way* for a new stadium.

ru: до сих пор, до настоящего времени
modifies: a whole clause, usually in the present perfect
contrast: Use the present perfect, not the present: *Up to now I've worked alone*, not *Up to now I work alone*.

senses.gloss: Until the present time.
senses.ru: до сих пор, до настоящего времени
examples: *Up to now*, nobody has complained.
I've done all the cooking *up to now*.
The weather has been great *up to now*.

ru: вверх и вниз; взад и вперёд
contrast: *Up and down the street* is a preposition use. Hyphenated before a noun it is an adjective meaning uneven: *an up-and-down season*.

senses.gloss: Upward and downward, again and again.
examples: The kids were jumping *up and down* on the bed.
The boat bobbed *up and down* on the waves.

senses.gloss: Backward and forward in the same place.
examples: He paced *up and down*, waiting for the call.
She walked *up and down* outside the office.

senses.gloss: From head to foot, of looking at someone critically.
examples: The guard looked me *up and down*.
She eyed him *up and down* and said nothing.

type: manner — with the top at the bottom
contrast: *Upside down* = top at the bottom (вверх ногами); *inside out* = the inside outward (наизнанку); *backward* = the front at the back (задом наперёд).

senses.gloss: With the top part at the bottom.
examples: You're holding the map *upside down*.
The bats hung *upside down* from the ceiling.
Turn the jar *upside down* and shake it.

senses.gloss: Into complete disorder, with *turn*.
examples: The police turned the house *upside down*.
Having a baby turned our lives *upside down*.

position: end — after the object; mid before *hope*, *doubt*, *appreciate*
modifies: verbs, comparatives (*very much better*), some past participles
contrast: *Very* alone cannot modify a verb: *I like it very much*, not *I very like it*. *Very much* goes after the object, not between the verb and object: not *I like very much jazz*. Mid position works only with a few verbs: *I very much hope so*.

senses.gloss: To a great degree; a lot.
examples: Thank you *very much*.
We enjoyed the concert *very much*.
I *very much* doubt he'll show up.

modifies: verbs; modal verbs in *may very well*
contrast: Alone at the start of a reply, *Very well* is a formal *OK* (хорошо, ладно) and sounds stiff in America. *I'm very well* uses *well* as an adjective (healthy).

senses.gloss: In a very good or skillful way.
examples: She speaks Spanish *very well*.
I don't know him *very well*.
The interview went *very well*.

senses.gloss: Quite possibly, after *may*, *might* or *could*.
examples: That may *very well* be true.
The price could *very well* go up next year.

modifies: a statement whose two parts can be swapped
contrast: Use it only when the same statement is true with the two parts swapped: *Cats hate dogs and vice versa*. For a plain reversal say *the other way around*; to reject what was said, *on the contrary*. All three are Russian *наоборот*.

senses.gloss: With the two things just mentioned the other way around.
examples: I help her with math, and *vice versa*.
You can drive from Boston to New York or *vice versa*.
Cats often dislike dogs, and *vice versa*.

senses.gloss: In addition, and more importantly.
examples: The hotel was cheap. *What's more*, it was right on the beach.
He's late again, and *what is more*, he didn't call.
The new phone is faster; *what's more*, the battery lasts two days.

position: front or end — or before its word (*without doubt the best*)
modifies: a whole clause; a superlative phrase
form: also *without a doubt*, more common in speech
contrast: *Without (a) doubt* means certainly; *no doubt* is weaker and often means *probably*: *No doubt he'll be late again* (наверняка).

senses.gloss: Certainly; with no reason to doubt it.
examples: This is *without doubt* the best pizza in town.
*Without a doubt*, she's the smartest person on the team.
He was the right choice, *without doubt*.

type: manner — in exactly the same words

senses.gloss: In exactly the same words.
examples: He copied the essay *word for word* from the internet.
Can you repeat what she said *word for word*?
Don't translate *word for word*; translate the meaning.

type: frequency — every week for a long time
modifies: a verb or a whole clause
form: the same pattern as *day after day*, *year after year*

senses.gloss: Every week, continuing for a long time.
examples: *Week after week*, the show topped the ratings.
She visited her father in the hospital *week after week*.
We ate the same meals *week after week*.

position: front — before a clause, or alone as a reply
contrast: Informal and very American. As a reply to *Thanks*, it means *you're welcome*: *“Thanks for the ride.” “You bet.”* It has nothing to do with gambling.

senses.gloss: Certainly; of course.
examples: *You bet* I'll be there.
“Are you coming to the game?” “*You bet*!”
*You bet* we were scared.
